title: Ghost scale signals scratchpad
content:
Quick summary:
- Trying to capture the weird "ghost" scale events where Dedicated GPU pool scales up (allocates instances / pods) and then immediately scales back down after 30–90s, leaving us with a lot of wasted spin-up and model cold starts. Observed across two clusters (us-west1, eu-central).
- This doc is a running scratchpad: commands run, raw snippets, rough hypotheses, short experiments to reproduce locally. Not polished.

Timeline & top-level observations:
- 2026-01-28 11:02 UTC: customer A triggered burst; autoscaler spun up 6 nodes in pool, 10 pods scheduled; by 11:03, 4 nodes reported NotReady and flapped, autoscaler removed 3 nodes; traffic returned (but many requests got 500s/timeouts).
- Events show repeated "scale_up" followed by immediate "scale_down" within 1-2 minutes (see events below).
- Not correlated to billing/scheduled maintenance. No obvious quota breach.

Commands & snippets I ran (repro steps and captures):
1) Kubernetes / cluster state
- kubectl get hpa -n redwood-serving
  NAME                   REFERENCE                  TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
  gpu-pool-hpa           Deployment/gpu-worker       0%/80%     2         20        4          3d

- kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu
  node-gpu-1 READY  4d  10.128.0.6    g4dn.xlarge  0/1 GPU_ALLOCATED=0
  node-gpu-2 NotReady 1m 10.128.0.7   g4dn.xlarge  0/1 GPU_ALLOCATED=0

- kubectl describe node node-gpu-2
  Conditions:
    Ready        False   KubeletReady    2026-01-28T11:02:33Z   Kubelet stopped posting heartbeat
  Events:
    11:02:33   NodeHasDiskPressure   kubelet  kubelet has disk pressure
    11:03:05   NodeAllocatableEnforced  kubelet  Updated Node Allocatable

2) Autoscaler traces (cloud autoscaler logs):
- Trace: scale_up request accepted (reason: CPU-based HPA target) -> provisioning started -> nodes reach Running -> kubelet self-reports DiskPressure -> cloud autoscaler marks node Unhealthy -> drain -> scale_down
- Sample autoscaler log entry:
  2026-01-28T11:02:20Z INFO scale_up: requested 3 nodes for pool-dedicated/gpu (policy=burst)
  2026-01-28T11:03:02Z WARN node_check: node node-gpu-2 reported disk_pressure=true; mark_unhealthy
  2026-01-28T11:03:45Z INFO scale_down: removing 2 nodes from pool-dedicated/gpu (reason=unhealthy)

3) Pod logs during the window (model server):
- kubectl logs gpu-worker-7f8 -n redwood-serving | sed -n '1,120p'
  [11:02:40.321] model_load: starting load checkpoint v1.9
  [11:03:00.900] ERROR model_load: failed to mmap weights: Input/output error
  [11:03:01.100] ERROR runtime: gpu driver lost connection (NVIDIA kernel panic?)
  [11:03:02.123] CRIT server: shutting down due to loader failure

4) Node-level system logs (journalctl -u kubelet):
  Jan 28 11:02:56 node-gpu-2 kubelet[1234]: Eviction manager: attempted reclaim 0kB, available: 1.2GB, thresholds: memory.available<1.5GB
  Jan 28 11:03:00 node-gpu-2 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1e): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
  Jan 28 11:03:01 node-gpu-2 systemd: kubelet: Node became NotReady (kernel reports)

5) nvidia-smi at 11:03 snapshot (node-gpu-2):
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | NVIDIA-SMI 525.76.13    Driver Version: 525.76.13    CUDA Version: 11.7     |
  |  GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
  |    0  Tesla T4     Off          | 00000000:00:1E.0  Off | N/A                    |
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  |  0  C   0%   34C  P0    20W / 70W | 0MiB / 15109MiB | 0% Default |
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  (but kernel logs show GPU fell off the bus right after)

Hypotheses (brain dump):
- H1: New nodes are provisioned with ephemeral storage too small for model checkpoint mmap and eviction threshold is hit -> DiskPressure -> kubelet marks NotReady -> autoscaler sees unhealthy nodes -> scales down.
- H2: Some AMI image/drivers are flaky on first boot for a subset of zones; first boot triggers kernel GPU driver crash (Xid events) -> kubelet NotReady. Repeatable in eu-central on 2026-01-31 with image v2025.12.
- H3: Workload shaping: HPA target uses CPU% across pods but small startup burst of big model load ups memory and ephemeral IO leading to local eviction triggers. Autoscaler sees increased failure rate and scales back. Need to confirm HPA target config vs actual startup resource footprint.
- H4: Race between prewarm and scheduler: prewarm/standby pods allocate GPU on node but do not finish init quickly; kubelet eviction thresholds computed while init loads -> transient disk pressure -> node removed.

Commands to reproduce / local experiments to run next:
- Repro A: Start a fresh node from the same image in a test pool, run a synthetic model load that mmaps ~6GB and hits disk IO (dd if=/dev/urandom of=/tmp/model.bin bs=1M count=6000) while kube-proxy + kubelet are running, watch for DiskPressure.
- Repro B: Boot nodes with debug kernel messages enabled, capture dmesg and journalctl continuously, try two boot variants: with driver auto-update on first boot vs pre-baked driver.
- Repro C: Adjust HPA target to use custom metric (model-load-requests) rather than CPU; reduce initial burst by adding startupDelayMs in model server to stagger weight loads.

Quick config fragments observed (copied from infra):
- autoscaler policy snippet: (note: informal copy)
  pool: pool-dedicated/gpu
  min_nodes: 2
  max_nodes: 20
  scale_up: policy: burst, cool_down: 30s
  scale_down: policy: aggressive, cool_down: 60s, remove_unhealthy: true

- hpa snippet:
  apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
  kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu
        target:
          type: Utilization
          averageUtilization: 80

Open questions / things to check quickly:
- Are image bake tests covering heavy mmap+IO workloads on boot? (ask platform/image team)
- What's the disk size of the ephemeral attached volume for the gpu instance types spun up? If < 50GB and models are >20GB, mmap and model cache could trigger immediate pressure.
- Is there a prewarm init container that writes logs to /var/log and fills disk quickly?
- Cross-check cloud provider health check wave: are these nodes failing provider-level health probes (e.g., instance agent) immediately after boot?

Slack threads and thread IDs to search later: #infra-gpu-pool (thread Ts: 2026-01-28 11:10 UTC, message ids: 3419..3427)

Notes to self (next steps):
- 1) Recreate small test pool with same image in eu-central; run Repro A + Repro B, capture serial console + kernel logs. (owner: Sofia)
- 2) Ask image-team for bake logs + diff between v2025.12 and v2025.10 (owner: Aisha)
- 3) Short-term mitigation: change autoscaler remove_unhealthy:false so nodes don't immediately get removed while debugging; extend scale_down.cool_down to 5m. Communicate risk of over-provision. (owner: Ben)
- 4) Evaluate adding a small init delay in model server to serialize mmap loads. Quick experiment: add sleep 5 at start of model loader, test cold-start throughput.

Random scratch thought: could the kubelet eviction manager be using ephemeral-disk metrics that are inaccurate for some AMIs? I've seen inaccurate "inode pressure" signals from older kernels. If so, nodes get flagged incorrectly.

Logs & copies saved to bucket:
- gs://redwood-debug/ghost-scale/2026-01-28_node-gpu-2_journal.log
- gs://redwood-debug/ghost-scale/2026-01-28_autoscaler.log

If someone picks this up: start with reproducer in test pool and triage driver kernel (Xid 79) — that kernel message often points to PCI bus instability (hardware or driver mismatch). Also confirm ephemeral volume size.

-- end of scratchpad --
